note: THE STEP RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1108).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, stated first because it is what separates it from
every other schema carrier in src/. The other schemas are read by a
validator and by nothing else: they describe a record the composing party
already knows the shape of. This one is read TWICE, and the second reader
is the point. `validateSteps` in src/compose.mjs reads the field set from
it, and the path-composition state of the Brief workflow table RENDERS it
into the judge's prompt. So the text the Model composes against and the
text the refusal enforces are one file and cannot disagree.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured on 2026-09-12 over the two live Briefs
(theses/calling-saved-permission-durable-leaves and
theses/steps-real-quality-matter-degree). No file declared the Step's
fields or what they mean. The composer inferred the shape from
.claude/skills/brief/SKILL.md's prose, wrote a Candidates JSON, and
`validateSteps` checked it afterwards -- so the only Harness text carrying
what a field means was a refusal string, seen only when shape had already
failed. Claim cardinality drifted accordingly: the first Brief carried 1
to 3 claims per Step, the second 4 to 6, with up to six claims from one
Strand in a single Step.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. Every MUST of the
composition design stays judgment-class and is judged at path review. A
missing field is refused here; a weak rationale is not, and no description
below is ever matched against a value.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.

what_a_step_is: A Step is one move of the Reader Path: the smallest unit that takes the
reader from one state to another. `Step = Input + State` -- the Input is
the material it stands on (its Strands), and the State is the Move it
binds, which is what names the kind of reader-state transition it makes.
A Step with no Move has no defined transition type and is not a Step.
The Step's shape is the field table below; The Step and the Move it binds is why `move` sits among its required fields.

step_id.description: This Step's own id, unique within the path. Other Steps address it through `depends_on`, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id.

materials.description: The Strands this Step stands on, as LessonDisplayIDs (`L<n>`). A Step with no material asserts nothing on anyone's behalf.

purpose.description: What this Step is for in the path -- the work it does toward the adopted Thesis, in one or two sentences. A VERB ABOUT THE READER, carrying no proposition from the material: a purpose that could be true or false of the world is a claim in the wrong field.

reader_state_before.description: What the reader holds when this Step begins. Judged at the specialization occasion against the Move's `requires`: a Step's before-state must be a consistent specialization of what its Move demands.

reader_state_after.description: What the reader holds when this Step ends. Judged against the Move's `effect` the same way. The two state fields are the Step's transition, written as the reader's condition rather than as the writer's intent -- the reader's CONDITION afterwards, never a proposition about the world.

depends_on.description: The EARLIER Steps whose conclusions this Step stands on, by `step_id`. May be empty. An id that is not an earlier Step is refused -- a dependency on a later Step is a path that cannot be read in order.

rationale.description: Why this Step sits HERE, at this position, rather than earlier or later. The ORDER ARGUMENT, not a restatement of the purpose and not a claim the Step asserts.

move.description: The Move library entry this Step binds, by id. The Move IS the State component of a Step, so the binding is required rather than encouraged, and the id is resolved against the Move library at adoption.

claims.description: What this Step ASSERTS, one entry per Strand it names in `materials`. A claim is a PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD and names no reader; a claim that mentions the reader belongs in `purpose` or in a state field. Its ground is the pinned Lesson, held as an address in the Brief's Strands section and never copied here. See `claim` below -- the cardinality rule is the part most likely to be got wrong.

journeys.description: The Journeys this Step draws on, each naming the Strand whose Journey it takes and what the Step uses it for. A Journey is MATERIAL THE STEP EDITS, never an assertion the Step must recover -- it carries no claim, Reverse Outlining checks no fragment of it, and the Step Packet renders it as prose to edit for the Move's purpose. Nothing here bounds how many a Step declares: a Step telling two cases for one claim is a path-review judgment, the way the number of claims is bounded by the Step's materials rather than by a number. See `journey` below.

entailed.description: True where a proposition this Step asserts is not explicit in the material and is reached by inference. The flag is the composer's judgment; the Harness refuses only a flag with no reasoning beside it.

entailment_reasoning.description: The inference itself, stated so path review and the owner can judge it. Entailment is interpretation, judged rather than silently trusted.

bridges.description: Present only on a Step inserted between two adjacent Steps during the revise pass; names that adjacent pair by `step_id`. It is disclosed at the Candidate-selection gate, so an unvalidated marking would render at an owner surface. The Bridge Step and the revise pass is where that insertion is defined.

introduces.description: Terms this Step introduces to the reader for the first time. The accumulated ledger the Step Packet renders is derived from these; whether a term is genuinely new HERE is a judgment and is not checked. The reader-knowledge ledger is the accumulation this feeds.

opens_section.description: Present on a Step that opens a Section of the finished article; carries that Section's name. The four grouping rules are a property of the whole path and run after every Step is known to be well formed. The Section grouping carries the four rules.

figure.description: The composer's statement of what a figure lets the reader hold here that the prose leaves hard to hold. The default is NO figure: a Step without this field has none and nothing asks about it. The figure decision is where the field is defined.

figure_roles.description: Binds every role of the Move's `visual_form` to one of THIS Step's own claims, addressed `g<n>` and numbered from 1 in the order the claims are declared. A role bound to another Step's claim is unreachable by construction: the address space is this Step's claims and has no syntax for anyone else's.

definition: A CLAIM IS THE ONE PROPOSITION THIS STEP ASSERTS ON BEHALF OF ONE
STRAND, FOR THIS READER AT THIS POINT IN THE PATH.
ITS GROUND IS THE PINNED LESSON, HELD AS AN ADDRESS AND NEVER COPIED.
In Toulmin's layout the claim is what is asserted and the ground is the
data it rests on; this field carries the assertion, and the Lesson it
rests on stays at its pin in the Brief's Strands section. The Lesson's
own Claim sentence is at that pin and is never rendered here or in the
Step Packet, which is what keeps `assert nothing beyond` checkable:
what the Step may assert is this list, and nothing arrives beside it.
A CLAIM IS A PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD AND NAMES NO READER. The
boundary against the Step's other fields is one of grammatical kind:
`purpose` is a verb about the reader and carries no proposition from
the material, `reader_state_after` is the reader's condition
afterwards, and `rationale` is the order argument. A claim that
mentions the reader, or a purpose that could be true or false of the
world, is in the wrong field.
ONE CLAIM PER STRAND NAMED IN `materials`. Two claims in one Step
naming the same Strand is REFUSED, naming the Step and the Strand. A
Strand that serves several Steps carries a DIFFERENT claim in each --
that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement, and it
is why the rule is per Step rather than per path.
WHY THE CARDINALITY IS BOUNDED AT ALL, measured rather than argued
(kogaki#1108). The Step Packet requires every declared claim to be
recoverable from the realized passage, and `claims-unused` fails the
Step otherwise. With cardinality unbounded, claim generation drifted
into composing the article's decisive lines wholesale and calling them
claims -- so the comparison the Packet performs stopped measuring
grounding and started measuring how much of the passage had been written
in advance. One proposition per Strand is what keeps a claim a claim
the Strand supports rather than a draft of the sentence that will carry
it.
A CLAIM IS ONE PROPOSITION DERIVED FROM A STRAND, AND NOTHING ELSE. The
type set is closed at `strand`. Inherited reader state belongs to
`reader_state_before` and to the computed `already knows` ledger; a
presupposed premise belongs to the Brief's Reader start. Neither is an
assertion, so a passage that realizes its Step correctly never states
one and the Blind Reader never recovers it.
The claims rule is the spec half of this definition; the mechanical half -- the closed type set and the one-per-Strand refusal -- is carried here and enforced by `validateSteps`.

retired_types.step_effect: inherited reader state, which is already carried by this Step's `reader_state_before` and by the computed `already knows` ledger
retired_types.reader_assumption: a presupposed premise, which belongs to the Brief's Reader start

type.description: The closed set above. Today it has one member, `strand`.

proposition.description: The claim itself, STATED -- a specific proposition this Step asserts, not a pointer at where one could be found. An untyped pointer is not a claim.

strand.description: The Strand this claim is asserted on behalf of, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Step's `materials`, it is where the pinned Lesson that grounds the claim is addressed, and no other claim of this Step names it.

definition: A JOURNEY IS MATERIAL THE STEP DRAWS ON, NEVER AN ASSERTION THE STEP
MUST RECOVER. A Lesson's Claim is a proposition, and the planning
decision is what transformation of it this Step asserts -- so it is
carried in the Brief as the Step's claim. A Journey is a narrative, and
how it is told depends on the Move being performed and on the prose
already on the page -- so it is ADDRESSED at planning and EDITED at
realization. That asymmetry is the whole of why this field carries an
address and a use rather than any text.
THE BRIEF CARRIES NO JOURNEY TEXT. The entry names a Strand and what
this Step uses that Strand's Journey for; the prose lives at the
Strand's served journey cite, which the Brief already renders in its
Strands section. No decomposition of a Journey happens at planning
time.
IT ASSERTS NOTHING, AND THE CONSEQUENCES ARE MECHANICAL. A Journey
generates no claim, so `claims-unused` never asks for it back and the
Reverse Outline the Blind Reader hands over carries no Journey field
to compare. What this Step may ASSERT is its `claims` list, and a
Journey placed here does not widen it.
THE USE IS FROM A CLOSED SET, in plain words, read from `uses` below.
It is what the Step does with the material, not a claim about the
world: a use outside the set is refused by `validateSteps`, and
whether the use chosen serves the Move is path review's judgment.
COVERAGE ACCOUNTING IS UNCHANGED BY THIS FIELD. Journey placement is
counted from `materials` as `<L-id>.journey`, where it was counted
before, and this field neither feeds that count nor substitutes for
it.

uses.illustrate: to illustrate this Step's claim with the concrete case the Journey tells
uses.motivate: to motivate the question this Step opens, with the event that raised it
uses.contrast: to contrast, showing the expectation the event broke

strand.description: The Strand whose Journey this Step draws on, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Step's `materials` -- named bare or as `<L-id>.journey` -- and its served record must carry Journey material, which is what the Brief's `- journey cite:` line records.

use.description: What this Step uses the Journey for, from the closed set in `uses` above. A use outside that set is refused.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether a rationale is good,
whether a claim is genuinely supported by its Strand, whether a term is
really introduced here, and whether the before/after states are faithful
specializations of the Move are all judgment-class: they are judged at
path review and at the specialization occasion, and a refusal from this
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule this paragraph is an instance of.
